- `dq-sched` is a DataQuality schedule that points to `dq-def` by name (`MonitoringJobDefinitionName`). It has no inline `NetworkConfig`, so the effective network settings come from the referenced job definition.
- `dq-def` has `NetworkConfig.EnableNetworkIsolation=false`. Monitoring containers launched by this schedule can make outbound network calls, so they aren't isolated.
- Because the schedule has no inline config, nothing overrides that value. The result isn't "not applicable" or "unknown".

I couldn't find an SM-13 definition I can confirm. I'm assuming it requires `EnableNetworkIsolation=true` on the effective monitoring job configuration. If your check defines it differently, such as only evaluating inline configs, the result could change.

To remediate, create a new data quality job definition with `EnableNetworkIsolation=true`, then point the schedule at it. Job definitions are immutable, so you can't edit `dq-def` in place. Before you switch, confirm the monitoring container doesn't need outbound access, for example to pull from S3 through a non-VPC path. Network isolation blocks that traffic.

I evaluated only the two responses you pasted and made no AWS calls. This assessment covers only `dq-sched`. Other schedules in us-east-1 would need the same two-step resolution, from schedule to job definition.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
